public_rationale: A March workflow explicitly retained human approval, supporting the claim about responsibility. It also automated bug finding and verification, so a literal claim of no engineering-task replacement would be too strong. Older research documents sycophancy and a possible training mechanism, but does not establish that the relevant coding tools deliberately flatter their users. The whole proposition is not settled.
limitations: The strongest contemporaneous workflow evidence comes from one vendor.
Company disclosures are not independent measurements of reliability.
Task automation, occupational replacement and human accountability are different measures.

statement.excerpt: It’s impossible to measure how many of each camp there are, but hearing Spotify’s CEO say that its top developers are basically not writing code anymore makes me deeply worried, because this shit isn’t replacing software engineering at all — it’s mindlessly removing friction and putting the burden of “good” or “right” on a user that it’s intentionally gassing up.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: isn’t replacing software engineering at all
putting the burden of “good” or “right” on a user
our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading concerns replacing the engineer's overall judgment and responsibility, rather than denying that tools automate individual tasks.
Good or right includes meeting requirements, correctness, testing and suitability for deployment.
Intentionally gassing up is treated as a claim of deliberate design or optimization for flattering users. Observed flattery alone does not establish intent.
Mindlessly is evaluative language and receives no separate numerical threshold.
For the ongoing state, the target is the current calendar month through the post date, the latest pre-post period in which workflows could be documented.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous workflow evidence shows that human users retain overall engineering and correctness judgments, together with evidence that the relevant coding tools deliberately flatter those users.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence shows reliable replacement of overall engineering responsibility in the relevant workflows, or directly establishes that the alleged deliberate flattering behavior is contrary to the tools' design and operation.

evidence.locator: Managing the review bottleneck, final paragraph
evidence.explanation: The announced workflow leaves approval with a human, supporting that part of the claim. The same disclosure describes automated bug finding and verification, so retaining responsibility does not mean that the tool performs no engineering work.

The demonstration assigns agents design critique, structural changes, performance work and documentation. It challenges a literal reading that no engineering tasks are being automated, but it retains substantial human management and predates the target period.

This research supports a mechanism through which preference optimization can reward agreement over truthfulness. It does not establish deliberate flattering design in the coding tools or period named by this assessment.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated deployment studies measuring which engineering responsibilities humans retain, paired with behavioral evaluations and design records addressing deliberate flattery in those same tools.
